articles.title: 러 군용기, 동해 KADIZ 진입 후 이탈…합참 “전투기 대응”
articles.snippet: 러시아 군용기 여러 대가 17일 오전 동해 한국방공식별구역(KADIZ·카디즈)에 진입했다가 이탈했다. 다만 영공 침범은 없었다. 합동참모본부는 “이날 새벽 러시아 군용기 수 대가 동해 KADIZ에 진입 후 이탈했으며, 영공 침범은 없었다”라고 밝혔다.합참은 “우리 군은 러시아 군용기가 KADIZ에 진입하기 이전부터 탐지했으며, 공군 전투기를 투입해 우발 상황에 대비한 전술 조치를 했다”라고 설명했다.합참은 러시아 군용기의 구체적인 기종과 대수, 비행 경로 등은 공개하지 않았다.방공식별구역(ADIZ)은 자국 영공으로 접근하는 외국 항공기를 조기에 식별하고 대응하기 위해 설정한 구역이다. 국가의 주권이 직접 영향을 미치는 영공과는 구분된다.외국 군용기가 다른 나라의 방공식별구역에 진입할 때는 사전에 비행계획 등을 통보하는 것이 일반적 관례다. 하지만 러시아는 KADIZ에 국제법적 근거가 없다며 이를 인정하지 않고 있다.한편 러시아 군용기는 올해 8월 25일에도 동해 KADIZ에 진입했다

articles.title: 李, 마닐라 도착하자마자 강행군…첫날 4개 일정 소화 [청계천 옆 사진관]
articles.snippet: 이재명 대통령과 김혜경 여사가 16일 아세안(ASEAN·동남아시아국가연합) 정상회의 참석을 위해 필리핀 마닐라에 도착했다. 이 대통령은 이날 마닐라 니노이 아키노 국제공항에 도착한 직후 정상회의가 열리는 필리핀 국제컨벤션센터(PICC)로 이동해 공식 일정에 돌입했다.첫 일정으로 아누틴 찬위라꾼 태국 총리와 한·태국 정상회담을 가진 뒤 아세안 정상회의에 참석했다.이 대통령은 정상회의 모두발언에서 “지정학적 갈등과 경제적 불확실성이 심해질수록 한국과 아세안은 더욱 긴밀히 연대해야 한다”고 강조했다. 특히 초국가 범죄 대응을 위한 협력의 중요성을 언급하며 “경찰 및 해양경찰 간 한·아세안 최초의 구체적인 사업이 실현됐다”고 밝혔다. 이어 “한국과 아세안은 온라인에서부터 바다에 이르기까지 양측 국민의 생명과 안전을 함께 지켜나갈 것”이라고 말했다.다음으로 아세안 정상회의 개최국인 필리핀 페르디난드 마르코스 주니어 대통령과 정상회담을 가졌고, 마지막으로 메콩과의 정상회의을 이어갔다.

articles.snippet: 강원 원주시가 성매매 집결지인 학성동 ‘희매촌’ 폐쇄를 민선 9기 핵심사업으로 선정하고 총력을 기울이기로 했다. 원주시는 희매촌 폐쇄를 지역사회의 시급한 정책과제로 보고 불법 성매매 근절과 지역 주민의 안전 확보를 위해 강력한 행정 대응에 나선다고 16일 밝혔다. 원주시는 그동안 관계기관 합동점검, 야간순찰, 성매매 피해상담실 운영 등을 추진한 데 이어 앞으로 건축, 위생, 방범 등 관련 부서 간 협업을 강화하고 적발된 위법 사항에 관해서는 관련 법령에 따른 행정처분 등 가용한 모든 수단을 적극 활용할 계획이다. 특히 7월 정부 관계 부처 합동으로 마련된 ‘성매매 집결지 폐쇄 추진 강화 방안’에 발맞춰 경찰과의 공조를 더욱 강화하기로 했다. 이를 위해 정부가 제시한 성매매업소 영업시간대 인력 배치 및 수시 단속, 성매매 장소 제공 건물주·관련자 수사, 범죄수익 추적·환수, 피해 여성 보호 조치가 현장에서 실질적으로 이행될 수 있도록 경찰과 구체적인 실행 방안을 협의할 예정이다.

articles.snippet: 국민의힘 장동혁 대표가 무소속 한동훈 의원의 장인인 고(故) 진형구 전 대전고검장 빈소를 17일 오전 조문했다.장 대표는 이날 오전 8시 30분경 당 지도부와 함께 서울 서초구 서울성모병원 장례식장에 마련된 빈소를 찾았다.장 대표는 빈소에서 당 지도부를 대표해 헌화를 하고 한 의원에게 인사를 건넸다. 이후 잠시 한 의원과 함께 식사 장소로 이동했다가, 7분여 만인 오전 8시 37분경 빈소를 떠났다. 일각에서는 장 대표의 조문 여부를 두고 ‘보수 통합론’과 연관 지어 다양한 정치적 분석을 내놓았지만, 관련된 발언은 없었다. 한편 전날 빈소에는 친한(친한동훈)계를 비롯한 국민의힘 의원들의 발길이 이어졌다.오세훈 서울시장도 전날 오후 빈소를 방문해 헌화 후 묵념했다. 이어 한 의원과 짧은 대화를 나눈 뒤 약 10분 후 장례식장에서 나왔다.오 시장은 조문을 마치고 나온 뒤 기자들로부터 보수 통합과 관련한 질문을 받자 “오늘은 드릴 말씀이 없다”며 말을 아꼈다.

articles.title: The Guardian view on Europe and Burnham: a future that can only be viewed through a glass darkly | Editorial
articles.snippet: Predicting a final destination for reset negotiations between the EU and the UK is futile, given the wider challenges that Brussels is facing At the European Political Community summit in Dublin last week, Emmanuel Macron was pictured apparently waving a grinning Andy Burnham to a seat at the head of the table, as Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, looked on. It was the visual equivalent of the “welcome back” message delivered by the French president in the early autumn, following Mr Burnham’s suggestion that rejoining the EU was an option for the UK to consider. At the time, Le Monde was among the media outlets to try out an updated portmanteau to mark the moment; mercifully, “Breturn” has yet to catch on. By Friday, the mood music will be louder still. A long-awaited reset summit is due to deliver the first fruits of Mr Burnham’s ongoing rapprochement with Brussels, in the form of new deals on food and drink, and emissions trading. A symbolically powerful youth exchange agreement is also in the works, although not yet over the line. But as they promote such adjustments to existing Brexit arrangements, the prime minister’s allies have been notably keen to avoid pre-empting the broader “conversation” that he desires on relations with the EU. articles.title: Milburn’s historic report on Britain’s lost generation says one key thing: finally, young lives will really matter | Polly Toynbee
articles.snippet: The year-long Neets inquiry has yielded a slew of new policies. But what matters is the political and social priority shift designed to change this country This week marks a monumental turning point for young people in Britain: finally they will come first, not last. It will mark an end, we must hope, to a perverse system that casts down the future generation and overrewards the already privileged old. There are 1 million Neets (16- to 24-year-olds not in education, employment or training) in the UK, and they are partly George Osborne’s progeny. He targeted the young, tearing down the Connexions youth service, careers guidance, youth clubs, family benefits and further education funding. Michael Gove, with his Gradgrind exam fixation, scythed through music, sports, arts, drama and technology – subjects that kept many engaged with school. Remember the playing fields sold, the leisure centres closed, the mental health services for Covid-scarred children cut back. That created a lost generation, but it’s worse than that: Neets are blamed and scorned for what older generations have done to them. Labour’s intent is to prioritise young people from babyhood. Let that begin here. Polly Toynbee is a Guardian columnist Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? articles.title: Killer tunes: how Grand Theft Auto conquered the music world
articles.snippet: Featuring hundreds of songs from the hippest real-world artists, the radio stations in Rockstar’s crime sagas are as hotly anticipated as the storylines. Contributors including Flying Lotus, Wavves and Nite Jewel reflect on the soundtracks’ curation and impact • The exclusive inside story of Grand Theft Auto VI • Crime pays: how GTA became a cultural colossus • Ten movies (and one TV show) that inspired GTA A droptop sports car speeds along a highway blaring 90s west coast rap from its booming sound system. Gradually, the asphalt gives way to rural backwaters, and so the sounds of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas’s local radio also change: less gangster rap and more twangin’ country – the grizzled croon of Merle Haggard and yearning warble of Patsy Cline. The Grand Theft Auto games are massive, stretching across many, many square miles of virtual terrain. Their soundtracks, relayed mostly via in-game radio stations, are manifold. And these two aspects, plus the personal experiences each player brings to the game, mean everyone has a different favourite musical memory from the smash-hit crime series. For acclaimed electronic musician Flying Lotus, it is all the hours he spent cavorting around 2004’s San Andreas that remain special. “It felt like the first time a game saw a different side of culture – black culture,” he says over the phone. “It felt like we were being seen. And with the extent of the music, all the cool California hip-hop, it felt like someone actually cared.” Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘I have to sell my bum on OnlyFans to go on tour’: Kate Nash on fame, feminism and fighting the music business
articles.snippet: She threw a (metaphorical) brick through Spotify’s window and exposed industry failings with her ‘Butts for Tour Buses’ campaign. Now the singer is embracing her Irish roots with her new album’s fighting spirit Kate Nash was standing on a fire truck in a showgirl outfit complete with white tights and pink G-string, shouting through a loudhailer about the music industry’s failure to pay artists fairly, when she wondered if she’d gone too far. It was 2024 and the truck, which made pit stops outside the London offices of Spotify and Live Nation, had a large black-and-white picture of Nash’s bum on the back along with the words “Butts for Tour Buses” – a reference to her newly launched OnlyFans account, which she was using to fund her tour. That afternoon, she called her manager Kat. “I told her: ‘I’ve thrown a brick through the window at Spotify.’ She went: ‘What, literally?’ and I said: ‘No, but I’ve been standing outside their offices with a megaphone, so that relationship is over. I don’t think we’ll be making their New Music Friday feature.’ And we didn’t.” [see footnote] Continue reading...

articles.title: Downstate review – razor-sharp tragicomedy set in a home for sex offenders
articles.snippet: Booth theatre, New York City Liza Colón-Zayas and Thomas Sadoski star in a provocative drama that brings nuance – and dark humor – to the stories of four child sex offenders Fred doesn’t get out much these days, thanks to the incident that put him in a wheelchair. But the elderly man finds joy in small things: the music of Chopin, fruity smoothies prepared by his doting housemate Dee, as well as Nutter Butter cookies. Not everyone sees Fred as harmless. Minutes after we meet him, a man a few decades his junior tells him that he is a fundamentally evil person and describes in cold, chilling detail exactly how he would carry out his murder. Fred is one of four registered sex offenders whose life in a group home is the subject of Downstate, a razor-sharp black comedy by playwright Bruce Norris. As well as Fred (Frances Guinan), the house residents include buff gym rat Gio (Al’Jaleel McGhee), taciturn Felix (Adrian Martinez) and the thespy, Diana Ross-obsessed Dee (K Todd Freeman), a surrogate caretaker for the old man. The men have been somewhat thrown together as an unlikely family, and the yellowing wallpaper and mismatched furniture has certainly seen better days. But the spot is a comfortable enough place for the men to land, although the baseball bat propped up by the front door shows that they are ready for violence if it comes their way. articles.title: The DCU’s James Gunn and Peter Safran are out – this is the biggest disaster to hit superhero movies in years
articles.snippet: The adventurous weirdness of the Gunn/Safran era that fans responded to is now history. Can the DCU ever get back on track? What was Warner Bros’ plan in 2022, when the studio decided to reboot its superhero output, jettison the increasingly muddled DC Extended Universe (DCEU) and replace it with a sparkling new DC Universe (DCU)? In part it was to wipe the slate clean after years of false starts, abandoned storylines and tonal lurches. There was a little bit of Marvel envy to proceedings, and quite possibly a desire to avoid having to ever again discuss Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice’s numerous failings. But mostly it was to take advantage of hiring of a man whom nobody could accuse of being short of ideas on how to make comic book movies. To a greater or lesser extent, the plan was James Gunn. Fast forward four years, and that plan lies in tatters. Gunn and his fellow DC Studios CEO Peter Safran have this week been fired (though they will reportedly stay on as film-makers), and Jeremy Latcham, another former Marvel man, is the new boss. What is the plan now? Nobody seems to know, and there is not much point asking David Ellison, the man whose Skydance empire has now gobbled up two of the former big five Hollywood studios (Paramount last year and Warner last month). That would be like asking for directions from a man who has just set fire to the map. Continue reading...
